title: RAW UNREVIEWED: name motivation constrains shared lexical writing without equating the named objects
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Complete owned Dioscorides IV.20 uses the related written plant alias μαχαιρίωνα and knife comparison μαχαίριον. I.1 repeats Iris in plant and celestial-analogy uses. A source-preserving lexical writing hypothesis must explain those form relations through one shared key while keeping the referents distinct; independent opaque name codes or object-equality glosses predict different consequences.

design.mechanism: A common source-language lexical writing key carries a name-motivating lexical base across a plant alias and an ordinary nonplant comparison term, preserving derivation/inflection alternatives and distinct referents.
design.unit: Complete previously owned Dioscorides IV.20 and I.1 source records. A future root-selected full admitted target unit plus at least two nonseed whole-unit consumers, under one fixed lexical channel. No target unit is selected in this proposal.
design.contrast: Shared lexical form motivation versus independently opaque object-name codes; resemblance/name motivation versus object identity.
design.prediction: Where the source-writing relation is claimed, the same key and bounded language-specific morphology must recover the name base in both name and ordinary comparison use. It must not transfer medicinal plant predicates to the knife or celestial referent.

exact_owned_inputs.IV.20: οἱ δὲ μαχαιρίωνα καλοῦσι διὰ τὸ τοῦ φύλλου σχῆμα ... ἄποξυ ὡς μαχαίριον
exact_owned_inputs.I.1: ἶρις Ἰλλυρικὴ ... ὅθεν διὰ τὴν ποικιλίαν ἀπεικάσθη Ἴριδι οὐρανίᾳ
exact_owned_inputs.interpretation: IV.20 explicitly supplies alternative plant names because of leaf shape, then compares sharpness with a knife. μαχαιρίωνα and μαχαίριον are related source-written forms, not asserted identical lexical tokens or a demonstrated inflection-only pair. I.1 supplies plant/celestial analogy, not an explicit assertion that a word was named after another word.

design.lexical_hypothesis: The manuscript may preserve a historical naming explanation through a language-level common lexical key rather than encoding each referent as an independently learned semantic constant. Whole lexicalized derivatives are allowed as paid entries only if their source-fixed relationship predicts a nonseed comparison use. No Greek or Latin target language is selected by having a Greek source.
unequal_consequences: Shared-key reading predicts a recoverable relation between a plant-name form and an ordinary comparison term in full prose; an opaque nomenclator can give those forms unrelated codewords.

A referent-equality reading would make a knife or celestial referent inherit plant-specific roots, dosage or effects. The source instead gives shape/colour analogy or naming motivation, so those predicate transfers are not licensed.

A translation that replaces the motivating name with an unrelated vernacular synonym may break the written relation while preserving general botany. That is a serious alternative, not evidence against all translation.
new_contract_vs_predecessors: IDEA357 and GDT963 already include these whole source records. The new consequence concerns lexical form relation across naming and ordinary analogy, rather than inverse widths or prefix-code existence.

GDT963 METHOD explicitly separates IRIS and CELESTIAL_IRIS semantic atoms. Its IV.20 PREDICTIONS row6 uses the opaque LEX:μαχαιρίωνα. Those choices permit different codewords without a shared spelling or morphological law. They remain unchanged; no new alias is donated to repair963.
IDEA810 relates one stem to spindle use twice. This offer instead requires related source-written lexical forms with different referents, rather than repetition of the same part-to-tool function.

IDEA622 already requires a shared channel for source-written Viola synonyms. These pairs are not synonyms of one plant: one member denotes or invokes a nonplant comparator. The new constraint must retain both lexical relation and referent nonidentity.
IDEA862 constrains p/y same-lexeme spelling by paragraph context. This proposal does not assume any p/y pair is one lexeme and does not reuse its contextual substitution rule.

smallest_possible_future_test.contract: Before any target reading, root chooses one explicit candidate source/target language relationship and freezes at most two independently justified source lexical relations plus the corresponding morphology/spelling rule. The source texts and their full order/duties remain fixed. Author one full already-owned target under that common rule; require two nonseed complete consumers with the same lexical base in ordinary comparison/name use. Score no isolated resemblance or snippet.
smallest_possible_future_test.discriminator: A separately written ordinary comparison occurrence has to be read under the common key fixed by the proposed name use. An unconstrained English alias for it is not permitted. Source shape/colour or etymology by itself cannot supply the target alignment.
smallest_possible_future_test.stop: If no admitted full unit and repeated base can be nominated, keep raw unselected. Do not build a source calibration, decoder, corpus or prolong963/1097 solver runs.

precise_missing_binding: An actual already-admitted complete target unit with both name use and ordinary comparison use, or a predeclared same-family relation across complete units. No actual target occurrence is nominated here.

A single language-level writing relationship that predicts the lexical base/affix relation, with source-word boundaries and all full-word residual costs retained. Greek source spelling does not identify Voynich signs.

Two nonseed complete lexical consumers and a independently fixed subject/reference reading that prevents automatic transfer of plant predicates to the comparator. Repeated strings alone do not establish this.
design.falsifier: Reject this exact source-preserving lexical channel if nonseed whole-unit derivations require unrelated free name keys, a new per-word spelling exception or changed stem boundary; or if the unchanged reading identifies the comparator with the plant and inherits incompatible source predicates. If the translation-language hypothesis does not preserve naming morphology, this specific channel is inapplicable rather than all semantic reading refuted. Missing target binding remains missing binding.
known_counterexamples: Name motivation may survive in a paraphrase even when a translation does not preserve the source lexical form; do not force all languages into the Greek morphology.
Related written forms can be separate lexicalized words, not one inflectional lemma. Both derivational and lexicalized analyses must be priced.
Shared source spelling can refer to different things; identical writing never establishes material identity or synonymy.
GDT608 whole-form residuals remain. No mandatory productive split, direct-letter alphabet, universal phonology or learned98-unit alphabet is asserted.

GDT963 remains bounded unresolved;1097 retains three solver-INFEASIBLE and four UNKNOWN local cases, no full code or independently replayable negative certificate. No source/compiler/code repair or runtime extension is selected.
GDT913 fixed lexicons and W93 missing name-comparison capacity remain as registered; this raw offers neither a recovered name nor a new owner.
design.access: Only existing owned primary prose and finalized reports read. No source fetch, target content query, image, reserve, new admission, contact, code, solver or experiment. f84/f84r remain sealed.
design.selection_status: Root owns independent novelty/selection review. RAW retention neither proves readiness nor reopens a failed model.
